## Highlights since 0.15.8

- **Import papers from Zotero.** Add papers can now browse your Zotero library, including its collections and sub-collections, and bring in the papers you pick.
- **Safer, faster Overleaf collaboration.** Your co-authors' edits survive conflict saves, remote deletes and restores. Typing at the same time as a co-author stays in live editing instead of falling back to a full sync, and Lattice sends its sync edits to Overleaf as live edits too. Syncing fetches only the files that changed instead of the whole project, and a co-author's live typing no longer rebuilds the PDF on every keystroke.
- **Review comments beside the PDF.** Read and answer comments in a column next to the PDF, and comment on a PDF passage from any source file in one step.
- **Review history with tracked changes.** A review mode in History shows changes as tracked edits you can accept or reject, with the changes marked in the PDF.
- **Better citations.** Notes link to the exact page of the cited paper, and you can add an optional "why I cited this" reason to each citation.
- **More ways to set up and write.** Choose the font, size and line height of the source and Markdown editors in Settings, clone a Git repository into a new project, and use Vim's `:w`, `:q` and `:wq`. There is also a new CVPR 2027 Rebuttal template.
- **Lattice for Intel Macs.** Each release now includes a signed, notarized Intel (x64) Mac build.

## Notable fixes

- Undoing an AI assistant edit keeps your co-authors' edits, and turns overlapping changes into conflicts instead of overwriting them.
- Annotations and bibliography edits are never saved over stale or unread text, and an audit of hidden state bugs fixed more cases like it.
- Overleaf reconnect, switching projects, stopping a build, Fix all and reloading the AI assistant panel no longer get stuck.
- Format document results and Overleaf's rejected edits stay tied to the right text.
- Files that still have conflict markers are not merged again, and fallback uploads to Overleaf are checked against their own history.
- Bibliography upgrades apply entry by entry instead of tidying the whole file.
- A citation card under a comment stays reachable.
- Citation suggestions stay open while you backspace through keys. Thanks to @ajay-mk.
- The AI assistant explains when your Codex is too old to list GPT-6 Astra.
- Linux users are told when a new release is out. Thanks to @knightnemo.
- The empty annotations panel is redrawn without "Return to file", the Git drawer's empty states are centred, and the in-app Lattice mark uses the icon's olive and sage.
- Developers: steadier perf-bench startup and Linux AppImage end-to-end tests.
